newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures finish session higher.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures finish session higher.

text.p: IMM currency futures finished higher, led by bullish followthrough in marks after overnight gains.

Traders said action was light to moderate overall, and said some players were on the sidelines ahead of key meetings this week during the International Monetary Fund (IMF)/World Bank spring meeting. President Bill Clinton and Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto will meet in Washington Friday and G7 finance ministers and central bankers meet next weekend.
Traders said dollar bullishness could stall this week as the market keeps its sights on those upcoming meetings.
The mark gained against French francs in cash trade as players fretted about French election and EMU concerns.
French President Jacques Chirac called for an early Parliamentary election for May 25 and June 1.

In an 1800 GMT televised speech, Chirac said an early vote was vital to prepare for major decisions on European integration, especially the "essential" single European currency. The decision was seen as a bid to ensure a safe majority before taking new austerity measures to qualify France for a single European currency in 1999.
Other traders said French election news was not so much the feature as was a pause in dollar bullishness.
"Face it, the dollar has been so strong for so long," an IMM trader said. He said dollar bulls were due to take a rest.
The mark's move began overnight, when June marks rallied to a two-week high of $0.5904. In the day session, marks extended gains to $0.5920.

"There were no real changes as far as the mood going into G7," an IMM trading floor manager said. "People are just looking to lighten up whatever dollar long positions they have." June yen, Swiss and sterling also ended strong.
Canadian dollar futures trade was very quiet, with only a 13-tick range seen. One trader said talk of a Canadian interest rate hike was beginning to fade.

At the close, June yen was up $0.000038 at $0.008047, marks up $0.0048 to $0.5913, Swiss added $0.0064 to $0.6977, sterling firmed $0.0030 to $1.6332, Can dollar up $0.0005 at $0.7178, Aussie dollar rose $0.0058 to $0.7781, Mex peso fell $0.000100 to $0.123725.
